heard: Four interacting galaxies share the sky with a supersonic imposter. Discovered in 1877 by Edouard Steffen, the group in the constellation Pegasus appears to be a tight cluster of five. However, modern measurements revealed that its brightest member, NGC 7320, is merely a foreground interloper. It sits only 39 million light years from Earth, while the other four galaxies are parked 210 to 340 million light years away. Even Wilder, another intruder named NGC 7318B, is currently falling into the center at supersonic speeds of several million kilometers per hour. This violent impact generates an immense cosmic shock wave bigger than the entire Milky Way. That colossal crash proves the true quintet is still taking shape. Where?
